detail.body:
Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Single-node device-side feature transport — provide an NPU-capable alternative to CUDA IPC for transferring multimodal feature tensors between local processes*).

## Motivation

`--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` currently requires NVIDIA CUDA: the feature pool, proxy lifecycle, and device primitives are hardcoded against `torch.cuda.*` and CUDA IPC handles. On Ascend NPU, multimodal features produced by the tokenizer process must therefore detour through host memory (CPU transport) even when both processes sit on the same node and the features already live in device HBM.

This PR makes the existing `cuda_ipc` transport NPU-capable with **zero behavior change on CUDA**. CUDA keeps the bounded pool + lease/ACK design unchanged; NPU follows the official torch_npu IPC recipe (`docs/memory_sharing_ipc.md`, method two): `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor` → `rebuild_npu_tensor`, using public APIs only (no undocumented ACL calls).

## Design

- **No new CLI option**: NPU reuses the existing `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` entry, gated per platform.
- **Features never leave NPU HBM**: the producer packs `(rebuild_func, args)` via the public `reduce_tensor` and pickles it into `proxy_state["ipc_extra"]["npu_ipc_payload"]` — a ~377 B descriptor regardless of feature size. The consumer rebuilds the tensor on its own device by redirecting the storage device index (`args[6]`), guarded by a layout/type check so an upstream layout change degrades with a warning instead of silently corrupting an unrelated argument.
- **Cross-device rebuild copies once into local HBM**: when the consumer rebuilds on a different device than the producer (e.g. TP2 on NPU), the redirected open returns a tensor backed by peer HBM through the IPC mapping. Compute reads work, but the DMA engine rejects host copies from that mapping (`memcpy exception`, 507001 — hit by the `.cpu()` inside `hash_feature`), which would abort the rank. Only in that branch the rebuild performs one D2D copy (~1.5 MiB per feature, microseconds); same-device rebuilds keep the zero-copy behaviour.
- **No pool on NPU**: zero HBM reservation, no lease/ACK bookkeeping; the KV-cache budget is no longer deducted for a pool that does not exist.
- **Platform code isolated in one inheriting pair**: the new `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc.py` hosts the torch_npu `reductions` patch import (single side-effect point), the device primitives, the pack/rebuild pair, and two classes. `NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy` **inherits** the existing `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy`, so every `isinstance` dispatch, pickle and msgpack path keeps working unchanged; it only fills the fields those consumers read and overrides the lifecycle hooks. `NpuIpcFeatureTransport` does **not** inherit `MmItemMemoryPool`: nothing dispatches on its type and the transport layer only calls `wrap_tensor` / `cancel_proxy`, so the NPU transport carries no pool, no lease/ACK and no constructor arguments. `cuda_ipc.py` itself is left byte-identical to `main`.

## Scope

Multimodal feature reconstruction has two paths:

- **Eager (shared path)** - 53 of the 56 registered processors. The scheduler rebuilds proxies before the model runs. All changes for this path live in shared code (`schedule_batch.py`, `mm_utils.py`, `base_processor.py`); no model file is touched. Verified end to end on Ascend with 9 families: Qwen2.5-VL, MiniCPM-V, Gemma3, Janus-Pro, Phi-4-multimodal, Kimi-VL, DeepSeek-OCR, GLM-OCR and Unlimited-OCR.
- **Deferred** - 3 processors (`qwen_vl.py`, `kimi_k3.py`, `kimi_k25.py`), used when the vision tower is DP-sharded and each rank must materialize only its own images. This PR adapts `qwen_vl.py` only (verified end to end on Ascend, TP1 and TP2).

`kimi_k3.py` / `kimi_k25.py` are not adapted in this PR: their reconstruction gate is limited to CUDA devices, so deferred reconstruction is not supported on Ascend when `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` is explicitly enabled. The default transport is unaffected. Equivalent one-line changes were prototyped and validated only via cross-process mocks; they were dropped because Kimi-K3 / K2.5 (2.8T MoE, ~1.56 TB weights) cannot be run end to end on the available hardware, and unverified code does not meet the bar for this PR. NPU support for those two families is left as follow-up work.

## Roadmap item coverage

| Roadmap requirement | How it is covered |
|---|---|
| Bounded memory use | No pool on NPU → zero HBM reservation; `kv_cache_configurator` skips the pool deduction on NPU, recovering ~2–3 GB of usable KV |
| Tensor lifetime | torch_npu ref-counter keeps the shared block alive while consumers exist; rebuilt tensors verified bitwise-identical even after the producer drops its source tensor |
| Cancellation | `cancel_proxy` handles NPU proxies on the processor rollback path |
| Pool exhaustion | Not applicable — NPU has no pool; the failure mode is `reduce_tensor` raising, which falls back to the CPU transport |
| Fallback to CPU path | `wrap_tensor` returns `None` on any pack failure → CPU transport; A/B runs show 0 fallbacks |
| Transfer cost & TTFT comparison | Benchmarks below |

## Modifications

8 files: 7 modified + 1 new (net **+315 / −49**).

**NEW** `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc.py` (217 lines)

- `NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy(CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy)` — inheritance is what keeps the 20+ `isinstance(..., CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy)` dispatch sites, pickle and msgpack decoding valid. `__init__` / `from_proxy_state` only populate the fields those consumers read (`npu_ipc_payload`, `reconstruct_tensor`, sync/borrow placeholders) and mark the consumer as acknowledged. `borrow_on_target_device` returns `None` so the scheduler falls back to reconstruction, `acknowledge_consumption` is a no-op, and `reconstruct_on_target_device` caches the rebuilt tensor per device.
- `NpuIpcFeatureTransport` — no inheritance from `MmItemMemoryPool`, no pool and no constructor arguments: only `wrap_tensor` (packs via `reduce_tensor`, returns `None` on failure → CPU transport) and `cancel_proxy` (no-op, there is no lease) are reachable.
- Device primitives: `is_device_tensor`, `current_device`, `_device_guard`, `_pack_tensor`, `_rebuild_tensor` (with the `args[6]` redirect, the layout guard and the cross-device local copy), plus the single torch_npu `reductions` patch import.

- `srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py` (+35 −26): choose `NpuIpcFeatureTransport` or `MmItemMemoryPool` per platform. The CUDA pool budget computation and its reservation log stay inside the CUDA branch, so NPU no longer runs the per-worker split (and `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB=0` no longer raises there).
- `srt/utils/msgpack_utils.py` (+10 −1): rebuild NPU proxies from `transport_mode` instead of hard-coding the CUDA class's `__new__`.
- `srt/arg_groups/serving_hook.py` (+27 −13): accept NPU for `cuda_ipc`; merge the two branch logs into one template, with the pool-handle cache note kept CUDA-only.
- `srt/managers/schedule_batch.py` (+10 −3), `srt/managers/mm_utils.py` (+4 −1), `srt/models/qwen3_vl.py` (+8 −4): resolve the transport device through `npu_ipc.current_device` instead of `torch.cuda.current_device()`.
- `srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py` (+4 −1): skip the feature-pool KV deduction on NPU.

`srt/multimodal/transport/cuda_ipc.py` is **not modified** — zero diff against `main`. On CUDA, every modified call site either executes identical code or is unreachable, so behaviour is unchanged (regression below).

## Benchmarks (Ascend 910, CANN 9.1.0, torch_npu 2.10.0, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking)

Transfer-level, two processes, 16 producer threads, in-flight depth 8, 800 frames per group:

| Feature size | CPU ms/frame | NPU IPC ms/frame | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5 MiB | 0.98 | 0.52 | 46.8% |
| 18.4 MiB | 13.07 | 0.54 | 95.9% |
| 47.6 MiB | 56.30 | 0.52 | 99.1% |

IPC cost is constant (~0.52 ms/frame — only the 377 B descriptor crosses processes) while CPU transfer is strictly linear in feature size.

End-to-end (4×1024² images per request, 16 concurrency, 90 s): 0 errors and 0 fallbacks on both arms; p50 delta −13.5% is within the noise band (p99 +11.1%, single round, transfer explains ~0.4% of end-to-end latency at this scale) and is not claimed as a win.

Accuracy: MMBench EN DEV v1.1, 1292 questions, CircularEval, greedy decoding, `cuda_ipc` vs `cpu` on the same node with a position-swap control over 3 rounds — no transport-induced accuracy delta (observed ±0.7 pp shifts do not follow the transport arm and flip sign after swapping dies).

## CUDA regression (unchanged behaviour)

Environment: RTX 4090 48G, Ubuntu 22.04, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.19.0, `sglang-kernel` 0.4.10, `--attention-backend triton`, TP1.

Method: dual-tree A/B (`baseline` = `c9bf6c84eb^`, `candidate` = this PR) × 2×2 matrix {baseline, candidate} × {default transport, `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc`}, one server per configuration, greedy decoding with a fixed seed, three request types (single image / two images / text-only) plus a 16-way concurrency round. Both paths touched by this PR are covered: `qwen3_vl.py` via a deferred-reconstruction model and the shared eager path via a model that never defers.

| Model | Path | Outputs (single / two images / text) | prompt/completion tokens | 16-way concurrency | `Using CUDA IPC` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct | deferred | identical in all 4 configurations (57 tokens) | 787 / 57, all 4 identical | 16/16, `distinct=1`, 0 errors | 0 (default) / 3 (cuda_ipc) |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct | eager | identical in all 4 configurations | 118/12, 217/3, 33/3 — all 4 identical | 16/16, `distinct=1`, 0 errors | 0 (default) / 1 (cuda_ipc) |

- Token ids are 100% identical across all comparison pairs; no `Traceback` in any of the 8 server runs.
- IPC switch is verified to be effective: the default-transport arms log 0 `Using CUDA IPC` lines, the `cuda_ipc` arms log the pool reservation line, so the comparison is not running an empty path.
- The only observed difference is a logprob jitter (±0.11 max) on the **first** image request of a server instance; it reproduces in the baseline tree with the same magnitude, and repeated requests within one server session are bit-identical, i.e. environment non-determinism unrelated to this PR. Token ids and texts never differ.
- Unit tests: 6 test files (IPC transport, pool budget, GPU feature transport, Qwen3-VL materialization) — 61 passed + 19 subtests, 0 failures on both trees.

## Test plan

- [x] `py_compile` on all touched files
- [x] Functional smoke on Ascend: real image request end-to-end, `NPU IPC rebuild success` in scheduler log, 0 CPU fallbacks / 0 tracebacks
- [x] Cross-process bitwise consistency of rebuilt tensors
- [x] Cross-device rebuild (TP2 on NPU): both ranks rebuild, image request returns 200 with the correct answer, no 507001
- [x] TP1 regression on NPU: same-device rebuild takes the unchanged zero-copy branch, 0 errors
- [x] 16-concurrency A/B (`cuda_ipc` vs `cpu`): 0 errors, 0 fallbacks on both arms
- [x] MMBench accuracy A/B as above
- [x] CUDA A/B regression on both paths (deferred + eager), 2×2 matrix as above: identical outputs, 0 errors

+"""Ascend NPU transport for multimodal feature tensors.
+
+The producer pickles the public ``reduce_tensor`` payload ``(reconstruct_func,
+args)`` and every consumer rebuilds the tensor on its own device with
+``rebuild_npu_tensor`` instead of mapping a CUDA feature pool.  Proxies,
+producer-side bookkeeping and device helpers live here so ``cuda_ipc`` stays
+free of platform branches.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import pickle
+import threading
+import time
+import weakref
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.transport.cuda_ipc import CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_npu
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_is_npu = is_npu()
+
+if _is_npu:
+    # Installs the reduce_tensor patches onto torch.multiprocessing.reductions.
+    import torch_npu.multiprocessing.reductions  # noqa: F401
+
+# Payload layout written by torch_npu's reductions patch: ``args[6]`` is the
+# storage device index, ``args[13]`` the IPC event handle and ``args[14]`` the
+# flag telling the consumer to wait on that event.
+_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX = 6
+_NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX = 13  # event handle; the next slot is the sync flag
+
+# Producer-side keepalive.  torch_npu releases an exported block as soon as the
+# producer drops its source tensor, which can happen while consumers are still
+# rebuilding it, so sources are held until their request finishes.  Module level
+# because proxies are pickled and shipped to other processes.
+_keepalive_lock = threading.Lock()
+# Wrapped features not yet bound to a request id (see ``bind_keepalive``).
+_pending_source_tensors: Dict[int, torch.Tensor] = {}
+# Sources held per request id until ``release_keepalive`` runs.
+_keepalive_by_request: Dict[str, List[torch.Tensor]] = {}
+# Bytes currently parked by per-request / not-yet-bound sources.
+_keepalive_bytes = 0
+_pending_bytes = 0
+# Count of features that fell back to CPU transport instead of IPC.
+_fallback_count = 0
+_KEEPALIVE_BUDGET_DIVISOR = 16  # at most 1/16 of HBM parked by the producer
+_MEMINFO_CACHE_TTL_S = 0.1  # mem_get_info costs ~0.4 ms on Ascend
+_meminfo_cache: Dict[Optional[int], Tuple[float, int, int]] = {}
+_REBUILD_LOG_INTERVAL = 1024  # sample the per-feature rebuild log
+_rebuild_count = 0
+
+
+def _device_mem_info(device_index: Optional[int]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return cached ``(free, total)`` bytes of *device_index*.
+
+    ``(-1, -1)`` when the query fails; the short TTL hides the per-call cost of
+    ``mem_get_info`` (about 0.4 ms on Ascend).
+    """
+    now = time.monotonic()
+    cached = _meminfo_cache.get(device_index)
+    if cached is not None and now - cached[0] < _MEMINFO_CACHE_TTL_S:
+        return cached[1], cached[2]
+    try:
+        free, total = torch.npu.mem_get_info(device_index)
+    except Exception:
+        return -1, -1
+    _meminfo_cache[device_index] = (now, free, total)
+    return free, total
+
+
+def _effective_budget_bytes(device_index: Optional[int]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return ``(budget, free)`` bytes the producer is allowed to park.
+
+    The budget is ``total / 16`` so exported sources never take more than a
+    sixteenth of HBM, then clamped to the currently free bytes.
+    """
+    free, total = _device_mem_info(device_index)
+    if total <= 0:
+        return 0, free
+    cap = total // _KEEPALIVE_BUDGET_DIVISOR
+    if free < 0:
+        return cap, free
+    return min(cap, free), free
+
+
+def bind_keepalive(rid: str, mm_inputs) -> None:
+    """Move wrapped sources of *mm_inputs* from *pending* to request *rid*.
+
+    Runs once the scheduler knows the request id; the sources behind the
+    proxies stay alive until ``release_keepalive(rid)``.
+    """
+    if not _is_npu or not rid or not mm_inputs:
+        return
+    global _keepalive_bytes, _pending_bytes
+
+    items = getattr(mm_inputs, "mm_items", None)
+    if items is None:
+        items = mm_inputs if isinstance(mm_inputs, (list, tuple)) else [mm_inputs]
+
+    tensors: List[torch.Tensor] = []
+    for item in items:
+        for field in ("feature", "precomputed_embeddings"):
+            value = getattr(item, field, None)
+            if isinstance(value, NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy):
+                tensor = _pending_source_tensors.pop(id(value), None)
+                if tensor is not None:
+                    tensors.append(tensor)

+        return
+
+    nbytes = sum(t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in tensors)
+    # wrap_tensor already reserved these bytes; only move the accounting.
+    with _keepalive_lock:
+        _keepalive_by_request.setdefault(rid, []).extend(tensors)
+        _keepalive_bytes += nbytes
+        _pending_bytes -= nbytes
+        logger.debug(
+            "npu_ipc bind rid=%s bytes=%d total=%d pending=%d reqs=%d",
+            rid,
+            nbytes,
+            _keepalive_bytes,
+            len(_pending_source_tensors),
+            len(_keepalive_by_request),
+        )
+
+
+def release_keepalive(rid: str) -> None:
+    """Drop the source tensors held for *rid* and let torch_npu reclaim them."""
+    if not _is_npu or not rid:
+        return
+    global _keepalive_bytes
+
+    with _keepalive_lock:
+        tensors = _keepalive_by_request.pop(rid, None)
+        if not tensors:
+            return
+        _keepalive_bytes -= sum(t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in tensors)
+        logger.debug(
+            "npu_ipc release rid=%s total=%d pending=%d reqs=%d fallbacks=%d",
+            rid,
+            _keepalive_bytes,
+            len(_pending_source_tensors),
+            len(_keepalive_by_request),
+            _fallback_count,
+        )
+
+    # Dropping the references only makes the blocks eligible; the caching
+    # allocator reuses them after the next collect.
+    tensors.clear()
+    torch.npu.ipc_collect()
+
+
+def is_device_tensor(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    """Whether *tensor* lives on the accelerator (NPU or CUDA)."""
+    return tensor.device.type == ("npu" if _is_npu else "cuda")
+
+
+def current_device() -> int:
+    """Index of the accelerator device bound to this process."""
+    if _is_npu:
+        return torch.npu.current_device()
+    return torch.cuda.current_device()
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _device_guard(device_id: int) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Run the enclosed block with *device_id* as the current device."""
+    ctx = torch.npu.device(device_id) if _is_npu else torch.cuda.device(device_id)
+    with ctx:
+        yield
+
+
+def _pack_tensor(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> tuple:
+    """Return ``(reconstruct_func, args)`` from the public ``reduce_tensor``.
+
+    Consumers unpickle the pair and feed it to ``rebuild_npu_tensor``.
+    """
+    from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor
+
+    return reduce_tensor(tensor)
+
+
+# Export granularity is the storage, not the view.  One request ships several
+# views over a single allocation; exporting each view would keep the whole block
+# pinned in torch_npu's limbo.  Export it once, then rewrite the payload's copy
+# of shape / stride / nbytes / storage_offset so every view rebuilds from it.
+_export_lock = threading.Lock()
+_export_cache: Dict[int, Tuple[tuple, tuple, "weakref.ReferenceType"]] = {}
+
+
+def _export_storage_once(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[tuple, tuple]:
+    """Export *tensor*'s storage once and return a per-view ``(func, args)``.
+
+    The cached payload is copied and its view geometry patched: 1/2 shape and
+    stride, 3 storage offset, 8 byte span, 9 offset in bytes.
+    """
+    storage = tensor.untyped_storage()
+    base_ptr = storage.data_ptr()
+    elem_size = tensor.element_size()
+
+    with _export_lock:
+        cached = _export_cache.get(base_ptr)
+    reused = cached is not None and cached[2]() is not None
+    if reused:
+        func, base_args, _ = cached
+    else:
+        func, raw_args = _pack_tensor(tensor)
+        base_args = _flush_before_export(raw_args)
+        with _export_lock:
+            if len(_export_cache) > 64:
+                for key in [k for k, v in _export_cache.items() if v[2]() is None]:
+                    _export_cache.pop(key, None)
+            _export_cache[base_ptr] = (func, base_args, weakref.ref(tensor))
+
+    # The payload mirrors the positional args of ``rebuild_npu_tensor`` (see
+    # ``torch_npu.multiprocessing.reductions``); only the view geometry differs
+    # between slices of one storage.  Copy first: ``base_args`` is shared.
+    patched = list(base_args)
+    patched[1] = tensor.size()  # shape
+    patched[2] = tensor.stride()  # stride
+    patched[3] = 0  # element offset; the byte offset at [9] carries it instead
+    # Byte span this view covers: 1 + (size - 1) * stride per dim.  Using stride
+    # rather than numel keeps padded / non-contiguous views correct.
+    span = 1 + sum(
+        (size - 1) * stride for size, stride in zip(tensor.size(), tensor.stride())
+    )
+    patched[8] = span * elem_size  # storage_size_bytes: this view's span only
+    patched[9] = tensor.storage_offset() * elem_size  # where the view starts
+    return func, tuple(patched)
+
+
+def _flush_before_export(args: tuple) -> tuple:
+    """Synchronize the producing stream and clear ``event_sync_required``.
+
+    torch_npu attaches an IPC event that dies with the source storage and that
+    the producer never waits on; once an early consumer drops its view, a later
+    one opening the payload fails with ``AclIpcOpenEventHandle 107017``.  After
+    draining the stream the data is complete, so clearing the flag (``args[14]``)
+    keeps consumers off the dead handle.
+    """
+    if len(args) < _NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX + 2:
+        return args
+    if not args[_NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX + 1]:
+        return args
+    torch.npu.current_stream().synchronize()
+    patched = list(args)
+    patched[_NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX + 1] = False
+    return tuple(patched)
+
+
+def _rebuild_tensor(func, args: tuple, rebuild_device_idx: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rebuild a producer payload on *rebuild_device_idx*.
+
+    ``args[6]`` (storage device index) is redirected to the consumer device.
+    A cross-device mapping points at peer HBM: kernels can read it, but host
+    copies fail with ``memcpy exception`` (507001), so the tensor is cloned into
+    local memory.  Same-device rebuilds stay zero-copy.
+    """
+    redirected = list(args)
+    producer_device_idx = None
+    if len(redirected) > _NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX and isinstance(
+        redirected[_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX], int
+    ):
+        producer_device_idx = redirected[_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX]
+        redirected[_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX] = rebuild_device_idx
+    else:
+        logger.warning(
+            "NPU IPC payload args layout changed (len=%d); "
+            "rebuilding on the producer device instead of %d.",
+            len(redirected),
+            rebuild_device_idx,
+        )
+    # Older payloads may still carry the flag cleared by the producer.
+    if len(redirected) >= _NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX + 2:
+        redirected[_NPU_IPC_EVENT_ARG_INDEX + 1] = False
+
+    with _device_guard(rebuild_device_idx):
+        tensor = func(*redirected)
+        if (
+            producer_device_idx is not None
+            and producer_device_idx != rebuild_device_idx
+        ):
+            tensor = tensor.clone()
+    return tensor
+
+
+class NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy(CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy):
+    """Consumer-side proxy for one tensor shipped through torch_npu IPC."""
+
+    def __init__(self, payload: bytes):
+        self.proxy_state = {
+            "ipc_extra": {
+                "transport_mode": "npu_ipc",
+                "npu_ipc_payload": payload,
+            },
+            "tensor_data": None,
+        }
+        self._restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_proxy_state(cls, proxy_state: dict) -> "NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy":
+        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
+        obj.proxy_state = proxy_state
+        obj._restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state()
+        return obj
+
+    def _restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state(self) -> None:
+        """Restore attributes from ``proxy_state`` after unpickling."""
+        ipc_extra = self.proxy_state["ipc_extra"]
+        self.npu_ipc_payload = ipc_extra["npu_ipc_payload"]
+        self.reconstruct_tensor = None
+        self._consumer_acknowledged = True
+        # No pool, but the msgpack proxy encoder still serializes these.
+        self.sync_data_meta = None
+        self.sync_buffer = None
+        self._pool_storage = None
+        self._borrowed_storage = None
+        self._borrowed_base_address = None
+        self._borrowed_device_id = None
+
+    def borrow_on_target_device(
+        self, rebuild_device_idx: int
+    ) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+        """There is no pool lease; consumers reconstruct instead."""
+        return None
+
+    def acknowledge_consumption(
+        self, consumer_count: int = 1, consumer_rank: Optional[int] = None
+    ) -> None:
+        """Nothing is borrowed from a pool, so there is nothing to acknowledge."""
+        return
+
+    def reconstruct_on_target_device(
+        self,
+        rebuild_device_idx,
+        consumer_count: int = 1,
+        consumer_rank: Optional[int] = None,
+    ):
+        """Rebuild once per device and cache the result on the proxy."""
+        rebuild_device = torch.device(f"npu:{rebuild_device_idx}")
+        global _rebuild_count
+        if (
+            isinstance(self.reconstruct_tensor, torch.Tensor)
+            and self.reconstruct_tensor.device == rebuild_device
+        ):
+            return self.reconstruct_tensor
+
+        func, args = pickle.loads(self.npu_ipc_payload)
+        self.reconstruct_tensor = _rebuild_tensor(func, args, rebuild_device_idx)
+        _rebuild_count += 1
+        if _rebuild_count == 1 or _rebuild_count % _REBUILD_LOG_INTERVAL == 0:
+            logger.debug(
+                "NPU IPC rebuild success on device %s: shape=%s, dtype=%s, "
+                "nbytes=%d, rebuilds=%d.",
+                rebuild_device,
+                tuple(self.reconstruct_tensor.shape),
+                self.reconstruct_tensor.dtype,
+                self.reconstruct_tensor.numel()
+                * self.reconstruct_tensor.element_size(),
+                _rebuild_count,
+            )
+        return self.reconstruct_tensor
+
+
+class NpuIpcFeatureTransport:
+    """Producer side: export tensors over IPC, keep them alive, cancel on abort."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        """Log the transport choice once at startup."""
+        logger.info(
+            "NPU IPC transport uses torch_npu reduce_tensor/rebuild memory "
+            "sharing; no feature pool is reserved."
+        )
+
+    def wrap_tensor(
+        self, tensor: torch.Tensor, *, use_pool_handle_cache: bool
+    ) -> Optional[NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy]:
+        """Export *tensor* over IPC, or return ``None`` to use CPU transport.
+
+        Reserves keepalive budget first (over budget => ``None``), exports the
+        storage once, then holds the source until it is bound to a request.
+        """
+        global _pending_bytes, _fallback_count
+        nbytes = tensor.numel() * tensor.element_size()
+        device_index = tensor.device.index
+        with _keepalive_lock:
+            budget, free = _effective_budget_bytes(device_index)
+            if _keepalive_bytes + _pending_bytes + nbytes > budget:
+                _fallback_count += 1
+                if _fallback_count == 1:  # static quota: warn once
+                    limit = (
+                        "physical free memory"
+                        if free >= 0 and budget == free
+                        else "device quota"
+                    )
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "NPU IPC keepalive %s reached (%d MiB effective, free "
+                        "%.2f MiB) for a %.2f MiB feature (held %.2f MiB); "
+                        "falling back to CPU transport; further features will "
+                        "do the same silently.",
+                        limit,
+                        budget // (1024 * 1024),
+                        free / (1024 * 1024) if free >= 0 else -1.0,
+                        nbytes / (1024 * 1024),
+                        (_keepalive_bytes + _pending_bytes) / (1024 * 1024),
+                    )
+                return None
+            _pending_bytes += nbytes
+        try:
+            func, args = _export_storage_once(tensor)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            with _keepalive_lock:
+                _pending_bytes -= nbytes
+            logger.warning(
+                "NPU IPC reduce_tensor failed (%s); falling back to CPU transport.",
+                exc,
+            )
+            return None
+        proxy = NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy(pickle.dumps((func, args)))
+        with _keepalive_lock:
+            # Bound to the request later; the source must live until then.
+            _pending_source_tensors[id(proxy)] = tensor
+        return proxy
+
+    def cancel_proxy(self, proxy: NpuIpcTensorTransportProxy) -> None:
+        """Release the reservation of a proxy whose request never reached dispatch."""
+        global _pending_bytes
+        with _keepalive_lock:
+            tensor = _pending_source_tensors.pop(id(proxy), None)
+            if tensor is not None:
+                _pending_bytes -= tensor.numel() * tensor.element_size()
+        tensor = None
+        torch.npu.ipc_collect()
